catalog_quote: In the Gorakor dialect, words often have a similar but different vowel from that used in Patep. However, it is difficult to set up regular sound correspondences, since sometimes it is a higher vowel and sometimes a lower one. ... Initial unstressed syllables in Patep always have the vowel schwa [ə]. It appears to be a neutralised vowel, since some of the other dialects have full vowels in that position. A further difference is that for some words, Kumalu, Mumengtein, and Pelenkwa have a different stress pattern, so that not only does the initial syllable have a full vowel, but it also receives stress.

new_statements.rule_in_words: No Gorakor-specific rule is stated. The survey (by the Patep fieldworkers, who elicited the Gorakor lists themselves) treats Patep stress as the reference (Patep: stress on the first full-vowel syllable, initial schwa syllables unstressed) and names only Kumalu, Mumengtein and Pelenkwa as having a different (initial full-vowel, initial-stressed) pattern for some words; Gorakor is not listed as differing. The stress-marked Gorakor wordlist in Appendix B is consistent with a Patep-like pattern (schwa-initial words stressed on the second syllable, full-vowel words mostly initial-stressed) but shows exceptions (ma'nun 'face', i'ya· 'stomach'), so any 'initial / first full vowel' reading for Gorakor is an inference from data plus omission, not a published statement.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said for Gorakor (Patep 1975 statement mentions optional final secondary stress in compounds, Patep only).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated for Gorakor; wordlist forms ma'nun 'face' (Patep 'manon) and i'ya· 'stomach' carry non-initial stress on full-vowel-initial words.
new_statements.domain_note: Comparative dialect-survey remark based on 190-item SIL wordlists elicited in isolation (citation forms) via Tok Pisin, 1980; phonetic transcriptions with primary-stress marks.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog gora1262 'Gorakor' [goc] = Adams & Lauck's (1985) 'Gorakor dialect' of the Mumeng chain (villages Gorakor, Timini, Bupu, Enggabuhu, Omala, Towangala, Perakles, Yanta; pop. 2,741 in 1979) = McElhanon (1984) '(35d) Yanta'; Glottolog lists Yanta [yant1237] as its only dialect. The survey's Appendix B rows labelled Gorakor (elicited from Gorakor-village speakers at Patep 2), Bupu and Perakles all belong to this variety. The only explicit stress rules in the chain are for the sister dialect Patep [pate1247] (Adams & Lauck 1975 sec. 5.2; Lauck Vissering 1993 p. 132),../pate1247/ -- they are NOT statements about Gorakor.
